newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bargain hunters give depressed Thai stocks boost.
newsitem.headline: Bargain hunters give depressed Thai stocks boost.

text.p: Bargain hunters from Japan, South Korea and Taiwan gave depressed Thai stocks a lift by late Friday afternoon as they picked up cheap issues following the market's plunge by over 4.5 percent earlier, brokers said.

The stock index had closed down 4.53 percent or 31.54 points by the lunch break to 666.42 on broad-based selling after a report that ratings agency Moody's Investors Service planned a possible downgrade of Thailand long term debt ratings.
At 0907 GMT, the index had recovered smartly to up 4.89 points at 702.95.
"Bargain hunters from Taiwan, Japan and South Korea bought blue chips in the banking and finance sectors purely for speculative reasons," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
There were also market rumours that unidentified Thai government agencies may have also been behind the latest round of buying to shore up the battered bourse, brokers said.
But there was no evidence to back this up, they added.

The market has generally been hit by the side-effects of high interest rates, a weak baht and talk that some financial institutions may have been hurt by the current Thai liquidity crunch, brokers said.
